qdrant_backups.s:
Highest-value item in this plan. Verified against the live cluster on 2026-08-04: `GET /collections/x2live` returns `"shard_number": 1, "replication_factor": 1`, and `GET /collections/x2live/snapshots` returns `{"result":[]}`. One disk failure loses every user, message and room. There is no backup script anywhere in scripts/.

PART A — snapshot script `scripts/qdrant-snapshot.mjs`:
1. Copy the env-loading preamble from scripts/migrate-named-vectors.mjs verbatim so QDRANT_URL/QDRANT_KEY resolve identically (it reads process.env; .env at the repo root holds them).
2. `POST ${QDRANT_URL}/collections/x2live/snapshots` with header `api-key: ${QDRANT_KEY}` -> `{"result":{"name":"x2live-<ts>.snapshot", ...}}`.
3. `GET ${QDRANT_URL}/collections/x2live/snapshots/${name}` (same header) and stream the body into R2 at key `backup/x2live/<ISO-date>.snapshot`. Use `wrangler r2 object put` from the shell, or the S3-compatible endpoint — NOT a Worker: a Worker cannot stream a multi-GB body inside its limits, which is exactly why this is a script and not a cron handler.
4. `DELETE ${QDRANT_URL}/collections/x2live/snapshots/${name}` afterwards so the cluster disk does not fill.
5. Exit non-zero on any failed step and print which one — a silent backup failure is worse than none.

PART B — restore drill, ONCE, by hand, and this is not optional: create a scratch collection `x2live_restore`, upload the snapshot to it, then `GET /collections/x2live_restore` and assert `points_count` equals the source. Delete the scratch collection. Record the observed counts in the commit message. A backup that has never been restored is a rumour, not a backup.

SCHEDULING: the ws worker already declares `"triggers": { "crons": ["*/1 * * * *"] }` in ws/wrangler.jsonc and calls back to /api/cron/dispatch-scheduled. Do NOT add a second cron trigger and do NOT run the snapshot from the Worker (see step 3). Run the script from a machine cron / CI schedule, daily.

REPLICATION: `replication_factor: 2` requires >=2 nodes on the Qdrant Cloud cluster — a dashboard and billing-tier change, not a code change. Do it if budget allows. The snapshot is the floor; replication is the ceiling. Ship the snapshot even if replication is deferred.

TESTS: a unit test here would only assert that fetch was called, which proves nothing. The meaningful verification is Part B, executed against the real cluster, with the counts pasted into the commit message. Do not fake a test to satisfy the four-phase rule — this step's phase 2 is 'run the restore and watch the counts match'.

user_empty_vector.s:
Every user row stores a 4096-element all-zero vector — 16 KB each, RAM-resident because the collection has `hnsw_config.on_disk: false` — whenever that user has no profile text. The named_vector_migration fixed this for messages (`vector: {}`) but missed users.

Four write sites, all currently writing `vector: { [V]: ZV }`:
1. src/lib/server/user.ts `save_user`: `await upsert(env, [{ id, vector: { [V]: ZV }, payload: u as unknown as Record<string, unknown> }]);` -> `vector: {}`
2. src/lib/server/user.ts `patch_user`: `vector: pt!.vector ?? { [V]: ZV }` -> `vector: pt!.vector ?? {}`
3. src/lib/server/user.ts `create_pw_user`: same shape as save_user -> `vector: {}`
4. src/lib/server/profile.ts `save_profile`: currently `const vec = text ? await embed_text(env, text) : ZV;` then `{ id: uid, vector: { [V]: vec }, payload: ... }`. Change to `const vec = text ? await embed_text(env, text) : null;` and `vector: vec && vec !== ZV ? { [V]: vec } : {}` — the `vec !== ZV` guard matters because `embed()` returns the shared ZV constant on any voxell.ai failure, and writing that is the same 16 KB of zeros by another route.

WHY THIS IS SAFE: AGENTS.md documents that since named_vector_migration a point may omit its vector entirely (`vector: {}`) at zero storage and index cost, and every message already relies on it. A profileless user is not a meaningful semantic hit anyway: src/routes/api/search/+server.ts only calls `search()` when `has_real_vec` is true and otherwise falls back to `scroll()`, so a vector-less user still shows up in unfiltered browse and in every filtered (gender/country/age) query.

TESTS FIRST: extend src/lib/server/__tests__/user.test.ts and add a save_profile case. Assert `upsertMock` receives `vector: {}` for a user with no about and no interests, and `vector: { t: [...] }` when embed returns a real vector. Assert the ZV-fallback case also yields `{}`. Run them against the current source and watch them fail with the received value being `{ t: [0,0,...] }` — if they pass before the change, the mock is wrong, rewrite it.

BACKFILL EXISTING ROWS (separate script, same commit): scroll `f(eq('s','u'))`, and for each point whose `t` vector is entirely zero call `POST ${QDRANT_URL}/collections/x2live/points/vectors/delete` with body `{"points": [<id>], "vector": ["t"]}`. Support `--dry-run` and default it ON. At the current 14 users this is instant; the script exists so it can be re-run later.

hub_message_table.s:
Foundation for moving messages out of Qdrant.

DECISION, SETTLED, DO NOT RE-LITIGATE: messages live in EACH PARTICIPANT'S OWN ChatHub Durable Object — the per-user mailbox model — not in a per-conversation DO. Reasons: (1) ChatHub is already on the delivery path, `/relay` already fires once per recipient, so the row insert costs ZERO additional DO requests, and DO requests are the dominant cost at volume; (2) `list_convs` collapses from a 2N-storage-read N+1 into a single GROUP BY. Per-conversation DOs were considered and rejected because any cross-conversation read would have to fan out. The cost is duplication: 2 rows per DM, N per group message. That is acceptable — DO SQLite storage is $0.20/GB-month and group fan-out is invisible below ~1,000 members. FTS5 is NOT needed and must not be added: all message search was deleted in finish_search_removal.

In ws/src/hub.ts, in the ChatHub constructor (alongside the existing `state.setWebSocketAutoResponse(...)` call):

  this.sql = state.storage.sql;
  this.sql.exec(`CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS m (
    id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, conv TEXT NOT NULL, f TEXT NOT NULL, t TEXT,
    gr TEXT, x TEXT, im TEXT, fl TEXT, rp TEXT, sk TEXT, rx TEXT,
    fw INTEGER, d INTEGER NOT NULL, e INTEGER
  )`);
  this.sql.exec(`CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS m_conv_d ON m(conv, d)`);

Column names mirror the `Message` type in src/lib/types.ts EXACTLY so no field-mapping layer is ever needed. `fl` (file attachment) and `rx` (reactions) are JSON strings — SQLite has no object type and both payloads are small. `fw` is 0/1. `e` is the edit timestamp, null when unedited.

WHY THE CONSTRUCTOR AND NOT A MIGRATION FLAG: the constructor runs on every DO wake and `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` is a no-op once the table exists. Gating it behind a stored `migrated` key would add a storage READ to every wake in order to skip a no-op — strictly worse.

NO NEW WRANGLER MIGRATION TAG IS NEEDED: ws/wrangler.jsonc already declares `{ "tag": "v1", "new_sqlite_classes": ["ChatHub"] }`, so the SQLite backend is already active for this class. Adding a table is not a class migration. Do not add a v6 tag.

TESTS FIRST: ws/src/__tests__/hub-do.test.ts — construct a ChatHub and assert `SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type IN ('table','index')` contains `m` and `m_conv_d`. Watch it fail before adding the DDL.

hub_message_writes.s:
Write messages into the mailbox. THIS STEP IS A DUAL WRITE — Qdrant keeps receiving every message unchanged. Do not remove the Qdrant path here; that happens only after migrate_messages_to_hub has verified reads. This step must leave the app behaving identically.

(1) INBOUND, in the ws/src/hub.ts `/relay` handler. It currently does:

  if (type === 'msg' && conv) {
      await this.bump_unread(conv, mute_key ?? '');
      await this.state.storage.put('conv:' + conv, { ... });
  }

Add the insert inside that same block, before `this.deliver(to, payload)`:

  this.sql.exec(
    `INSERT OR IGNORE INTO m (id, conv, f, t, gr, x, im, fl, rp, sk, rx, fw, d) VALUES (?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?)`,
    body.id, conv, body.from, body.to ?? null, body.group ?? null, body.text ?? '',
    body.image ?? null, body.file ? JSON.stringify(body.file) : null, body.reply_msg ?? null,
    body.sticker ?? null, null, body.fw ? 1 : 0, body.ts
  );

`INSERT OR IGNORE` because a relay can be retried and the message id is the primary key, so a replay is a harmless no-op. Note the relay payload field is `reply_msg` (see `build_relay_payload`), not `rp` — getting this wrong silently drops every reply reference.

(2) THE SENDER'S OWN COPY. src/routes/api/send/+server.ts already calls `hub_conv(...)` on `locals.bg` to self-index the conversation. Extend `hub_conv` in src/lib/server/hub_client.ts and the `/conv` handler in ws/src/hub.ts to carry the full message fields and perform the same INSERT. WITHOUT THIS THE SENDER SEES AN EMPTY THREAD — the relay deliberately excludes the sender (`g.members.filter((u) => u !== me.id)`), so nothing else would ever write their own outbound messages.

(3) EDITS, DELETES, REACTIONS already relay to every participant via `build_relay_payload` (`type: 'edit' | 'delete' | 'reaction'`). Extend those branches in the `/relay` handler:
  - edit:     `UPDATE m SET x = ?, e = ? WHERE id = ?`  (body.text, body.e, body.id)
  - delete:   `DELETE FROM m WHERE id = ?`
  - reaction: `UPDATE m SET rx = ? WHERE id = ?`  (JSON.stringify(body.rx))
TRAP: src/routes/api/messages/[id]/delete/+server.ts relays to `targets` which EXCLUDES the author — `g.members.filter((u) => u !== result.f)` for groups, and `[result.t]` for DMs. The author must be added to that list or their own copy is never deleted and the message reappears for them on reload.

TESTS FIRST, ws/src/__tests__/hub-do.test.ts: relay a msg then `SELECT * FROM m` and assert every column including a JSON-round-tripped `fl`; relay the same id twice and assert exactly one row; relay a msg with `reply_msg` set and assert `rp` is populated; relay edit/delete/reaction and assert the row changes. Add a src/routes/api/send test asserting the sender's own hub receives the full-field `/conv` call. Watch all of them fail first.

migrate_messages_to_hub.s:
One-off script `scripts/migrate-messages-to-hub.mjs`. Moves existing messages out of Qdrant into every participant's ChatHub, DECRYPTING AS IT GOES. This must run BEFORE drop_message_encryption — after that step the key is gone and every historical `enc:` message is unreadable forever.

For each Qdrant point with `s === 'm'` (paged scroll, `with_payload: true`, `with_vector: false`):
1. If `x` starts with `enc:`, decrypt it. Port the AES-GCM logic from src/lib/server/msg_crypto.ts VERBATIM — base64-decode after the `enc:` prefix, first 12 bytes are the IV, remainder is the ciphertext, key is `MESSAGE_ENC_KEY` base64-decoded and imported as raw AES-GCM. Read the key from process.env. Keep the `if (!stored.startsWith('enc:')) return stored;` tolerance: pre-encryption plaintext rows exist and must pass through untouched.
2. Derive the recipient set. DM -> `[m.f, m.t]`. Group -> the `mb` array from the `s='g'` point whose id is `m.gr` (fetch and cache these; there are only a handful).
3. POST the decrypted row to `/hub/<uid>/conv` — the full-field variant added in hub_message_writes — once per uid in that set, with the shared `SECRET` as a bearer token, matching how src/lib/server/hub_client.ts authenticates.

FLAGS: `--dry-run` printing per-uid row counts and writing nothing, defaulted ON so `--commit` is required to write; and `--since <ts>` so a second pass can sweep anything written during the cutover window.

SCALE NOTE: the live collection holds 197 points total, 167 carrying a `c` index. This is minutes of work today and hours in six months. Run it soon; the cost of this step only grows.

VERIFICATION BEFORE CUTOVER, mandatory: pick five conversations spanning at least one DM and one group, call `/hub/<uid>/msgs?conv=<c>` and diff against `get_messages` reading from Qdrant. Require byte-identical text, identical ids, identical ordering. ONLY THEN remove the Qdrant `upsert` from `send_msg`/`send_group_msg` and the Qdrant reads from `page_msgs`/`get_message` in src/lib/server/chat.ts.

DO NOT delete the message points from Qdrant in the same commit as the cutover. Leave them in place; delete them in a separate change after a week of the mailbox serving live reads. Those points are the rollback.

TESTS FIRST: unit-test the decrypt port against a ciphertext produced by the current `encrypt_text` (round-trip), and against a plaintext row (passes through). Unit-test recipient-set derivation for a DM and for a group with three members. The migration run itself is verified by the five-conversation diff above, not by a unit test — that diff IS phase 4 for this step.

drop_message_encryption.s:
Remove app-level message encryption. Decided by the user; do not re-argue it. For the record in the commit message: Durable Object storage is already AES-256 encrypted at rest by Cloudflare automatically and with no configuration (https://developers.cloudflare.com/durable-objects/reference/data-security/), so this removes one layer rather than all of them. What is given up is protection against a Cloudflare-side compromise or a leaked Durable Object.

HARD ORDERING CONSTRAINT: this step MUST run AFTER migrate_messages_to_hub has decrypted and moved the existing rows. If migrate_messages_to_hub is not marked done, STOP and tell the user — running this first makes every historical message permanently unreadable.

DELETE:
- src/lib/server/msg_crypto.ts and src/lib/server/__tests__/msg_crypto.test.ts
- in src/lib/server/chat.ts: the `import { encrypt_text, decrypt_text } from './msg_crypto';` line, and every call — `x: await encrypt_text(env, text)` becomes `x: text` in `send_msg` and `send_group_msg`; `x: await encrypt_text(env, new_text)` becomes `x: new_text` in `edit_msg`; `x: await decrypt_text(env, m.x)` becomes `m.x` in `page_msgs` and `get_message`. Once decrypt_text is gone from `page_msgs`, that whole `Promise.all(pts.map(async ...))` collapses to a plain `.map()` — simplify it rather than leaving a pointless async map.
- the `MESSAGE_ENC_KEY` entry from `secrets_store_secrets` in wrangler.jsonc
- `MESSAGE_ENC_KEY?: SecretVal;` from the `QEnv` type in src/lib/server/qdrant.ts
- the `vi.mock('../msg_crypto', ...)` block and every `'enc:'` expectation in src/lib/server/__tests__/chat.test.ts, src/lib/server/__tests__/chat-edit.test.ts and src/lib/server/__tests__/scheduled.test.ts

Leave the secret itself in the Cloudflare Secrets Store until the migration has been verified in production for a few days, then remove it with `wrangler secrets-store secret delete`. Deleting the binding from wrangler.jsonc is enough to stop using it.

DO NOT strip the `if (!stored.startsWith('enc:')) return stored;` tolerance from scripts/migrate-messages-to-hub.mjs — that script must keep working on legacy rows if it ever needs a re-run before the key is destroyed.

TESTS FIRST: the three suites above currently assert `x: 'enc:hi there'` and similar throughout. Invert every one to assert plaintext (`x: 'hi there'`). Watch them fail against the current source, then delete the encryption and watch them pass.

media_signed_urls.s:
src/routes/media/[...key]/+server.ts serves two ways: a signed URL (`?e=<exp>&s=<sig>`), or a cookie-authenticated read for a logged-in user. Message payloads only ever build the UNSIGNED form — `/media/${image}` in src/routes/api/send/+server.ts, `media_url` in src/lib/server/media.ts, `media_src` in src/lib/attach.ts. So every image view runs a Worker and re-reads R2, and because the response depends on a cookie the edge cannot cache it. `signed_media_url` exists, is already tested, and is dead code on this path.

CHANGE: emit a signed URL from the send path. `sign_key(secret, key, exp)` and `signed_media_url(key, exp, sig)` in src/lib/server/media.ts are already written — use them. For message attachments use a long expiry (1 year) rather than the 24h `put_image` currently uses: the URL is stored inside the message and must keep working for as long as the message exists. Then DELETE the cookie branch from the media route so there is exactly one way in, and the route becomes fully edge-cacheable.

TRADE-OFF for the commit message: a signed URL is bearer-style — anyone holding it can fetch the object until it expires. That is already true of the existing signed path; making it the only path does not weaken anything. It stops the cookie branch pretending to add privacy while making every response uncacheable.

ALSO IN THIS STEP — the R2 orphan leak: `delete_image` in src/lib/server/media.ts is never called from any route. `delete_msg` returns `{ media_key, ... }` and src/routes/api/messages/[id]/delete/+server.ts assigns it to `result` and ignores `result.media_key`, so every deleted image stays in R2 forever. Call `delete_image(platform.env.MEDIA, locals.user.id, result.media_key)` when `media_key` is set. `delete_image` already enforces the `${uid}/` key prefix itself, so passing the caller's uid is the whole authorisation check.

TESTS FIRST: src/routes/media/__tests__/server.test.ts — an unsigned request now 403s rather than 401s or succeeding; a valid signature serves the object; an expired signature 403s; a tampered signature 403s. In the delete-route test, assert `delete_image` is called with the media key, and NOT called when the message had no image. Watch them fail first.

retention_and_orphans.s:
Nothing in this app ever deletes anything: no message TTL, no R2 lifecycle rule, no archive tier. Storage cost is rate x time and grows without bound, and there is no mechanism to satisfy a deletion request.

BLOCKING QUESTION FIRST: the retention window is a product decision, not an engineering one — forever, one year, or user-configurable. ASK THE USER before implementing (b). Do not pick a number silently.

(a) R2 lifecycle rule on the `x2-media` bucket: transition objects to Infrequent Access after 30 days. This is a dashboard / `wrangler r2 bucket lifecycle` setting with no code, and it is the cheapest win in this whole plan. Do it regardless of the answer to the question above.

(b) Message retention in ChatHub. Add a daily DO alarm (`this.state.storage.setAlarm`) whose handler runs `DELETE FROM m WHERE d < ?` with the cutoff, then reschedules itself for +24h. Put the window in a module-scope constant (`const RETENTION_MS = ...`) so changing it is one edit. WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND COST: the per-Durable-Object SQLite cap is 10 GB. A normal user at 50 messages/day would need over a thousand years to reach it, but a user in ~200 busy groups accumulates roughly 100K rows/day under the mailbox model and reaches 10 GB in months. This alarm is the mitigation for that specific ceiling.

(c) R2 orphan sweep for objects whose message no longer exists — a script under scripts/, run rarely and by hand, not a live path. Only needed for objects orphaned before media_signed_urls fixed the delete path.

TESTS FIRST: ws/src/__tests__/hub-do.test.ts — insert rows either side of the cutoff, fire the alarm handler, assert only the old rows are gone, assert the surviving rows are untouched, and assert the alarm rescheduled itself roughly 24h out. Watch them fail before the handler exists.

staging_and_metrics.s:
(a) STAGING. wrangler.jsonc and ws/wrangler.jsonc each define exactly one environment, both with `workers_dev: true`, so every deploy lands directly on production users. Add an `env.staging` block to both: distinct worker names (`x2-staging`, `x2-ws-staging`), a staging `WS_ORIGIN` pointing at the staging ws worker, and a `QDRANT_COLLECTION` var so staging writes to a separate collection. That last part requires making `C` in src/lib/server/qdrant.ts read from env rather than being the hardcoded `export const C = 'x2live';` — thread it through `QEnv` with `'x2live'` as the default so production behaviour is unchanged. Deploy with `wrangler deploy --env staging`. TRAP already documented in this repo: `wrangler deploy` overwrites dashboard-set vars with whatever the config says on every push, so both `WS_ORIGIN` values must be committed, never left blank.

(b) FOUR NUMBERS. Not a metrics platform — four, on one screen:
  1. send success rate — 200s vs 503s from /api/send. This is the only number that truly matters: did the message get stored.
  2. delivery p99 — send timestamp to the recipient's websocket frame.
  3. hub error rate — ChatHubError broken down by `reason` (network / http_<status> / bad_shape).
  4. Qdrant error rate — specifically the swallow-to-empty path in src/lib/server/qdrant.ts (`scroll`/`search`/`retrieve_one` all `.catch(() => [])`). This is the failure mode that presents to users as data loss, and today it is completely invisible.
Use Workers Analytics Engine: one binding plus a `writeDataPoint` call per event, read from the Cloudflare dashboard. Do not build anything else.

(c) LOGGING. src/lib/server/hub_client.ts `call()` logs EVERY hub call with a uid prefix, path and timing:
  console.log(`[HUB] ${init?.method ?? 'GET'} /hub/${uid.slice(0, 8)}${path} -> ${res.status} ${Date.now() - started}ms`);
Drop it to failure-only (`if (!res.ok) console.error(...)`). At volume that firehose costs more than the compute it is measuring. Same treatment for the `[WS-CLIENT]` per-message console.logs in src/lib/ws.ts — they run on every frame in every user's browser.

TESTS FIRST: assert `writeDataPoint` is called with the expected shape on a failed send and exactly once; assert the hub_client success path emits no console.log (spy on it) while a failure emits one console.error. Watch them fail first.
